leaders.name: Dallin H. Oaks
leaders.calling: President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
leaders.apostleDateNote: Bio: 'sustained as a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles on April 7, 1984.' Set apart as Church President October 14, 2025.
leaders.formerCareerDetail: He was a law clerk at the U.S. Supreme Court, a law professor at the University of Chicago, president of Brigham Young University (1971–1980), and a justice of the Utah Supreme Court when he was called as an Apostle.
leaders.funFact: He was called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles on the same day as President Russell M. Nelson in 1984.

leaders.name: Henry B. Eyring
leaders.calling: First Counselor in the First Presidency
leaders.callingNote: Also sustained (April 4, 2026 solemn assembly) as President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles; because he serves in the First Presidency, Uchtdorf serves as Acting President.
leaders.apostleDateNote: From Newsroom article president-oaks-new-first-presidency: 'sustained as a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles on April 1, 1995.'
leaders.formerCareerDetail: He taught at Stanford University's Graduate School of Business and was president of Ricks College in Rexburg, Idaho.
leaders.funFact: His first college degree was in physics, from the University of Utah.

leaders.name: D. Todd Christofferson
leaders.calling: Second Counselor in the First Presidency
leaders.apostleDateNote: Bio says 'called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles on April 5, 2008' (a general conference Saturday).
leaders.formerCareerDetail: He was a lawyer for banks, including associate general counsel of NationsBank (now Bank of America), and earlier was a law clerk to Judge John J. Sirica during the Watergate trials.
leaders.funFact: He served as a U.S. Army Reserve officer from 1971 to 1979, reaching the rank of captain, and served a mission in Argentina as a young man.

leaders.name: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
leaders.calling: Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
leaders.callingNote: Set apart as Acting President January 8, 2026 (after President Holland's death). 'Acting' because President Eyring, the senior Apostle outside the Church President, is President of the Quorum but serves in the First Presidency.
leaders.formerCareerDetail: After six years as a fighter pilot in the German Air Force, he flew for Lufthansa German Airlines, becoming its chief pilot and senior vice president of flight operations.
leaders.funFact: As a boy, his family had to flee their home twice — near the end of World War II and again in 1952 — before settling in Frankfurt, Germany.

leaders.name: David A. Bednar
leaders.calling: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
leaders.apostleDateNote: Bio gives only the ordination date (October 7, 2004); sustaining date not stated on the page.
leaders.formerCareerDetail: He was a professor of business management at Texas Tech University and the University of Arkansas, then president of BYU–Idaho (formerly Ricks College) from 1997 to 2004.
leaders.funFact: He served a full-time mission in Southern Germany.

leaders.name: Quentin L. Cook
leaders.calling: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
leaders.formerCareerDetail: He was a business lawyer and managing partner of a San Francisco Bay Area law firm, then president and CEO of a California health care system and vice chairman of Sutter Health.
leaders.funFact: He served a full-time mission in the British Mission.

leaders.name: Neil L. Andersen
leaders.calling: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
leaders.apostleDateNote: Bio: 'named an Apostle ... on April 4, 2009' (general conference Saturday).
leaders.formerCareerDetail: After earning an MBA from Harvard, he settled in Tampa, Florida, where his business interests included advertising, real estate development, and health care.
leaders.funFact: He grew up on a farm outside Pocatello, Idaho, and speaks French, Portuguese, and Spanish in addition to English.

leaders.name: Ronald A. Rasband
leaders.calling: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
leaders.apostleDateNote: Bio says 'called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles on October 3, 2015' (same conference session at which Stevenson and Renlund were sustained).
leaders.birthplace: Salt Lake City, Utah, United States
leaders.formerCareerDetail: He started at Huntsman Container Company as a sales representative in 1976 and became president and chief operating officer of Huntsman Chemical Corporation in 1987.
leaders.funFact: He served a mission in the Eastern States Mission and was once a missionary tour guide on Temple Square.

leaders.name: Gary E. Stevenson
leaders.calling: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
leaders.formerCareerDetail: He cofounded ICON Health & Fitness, Inc., an exercise equipment manufacturer, and served as its president and chief operating officer until 2008.
leaders.funFact: He served a mission in Japan (Fukuoka) and later returned as president of the Japan Nagoya Mission; he was raised in Cache Valley, Utah.

leaders.name: Dale G. Renlund
leaders.calling: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
leaders.birthplace: Salt Lake City, Utah, United States
leaders.formerCareerDetail: A medical doctor trained at Johns Hopkins, he was a professor of medicine at the University of Utah and medical director of the Utah heart transplant program.
leaders.funFact: He served a full-time mission in Sweden.

leaders.name: Gerrit W. Gong
leaders.calling: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
leaders.formerCareerDetail: A Rhodes Scholar with a doctorate from Oxford, he worked for the U.S. State Department, as special assistant to the U.S. ambassador in Beijing, at a Washington, DC, think tank, and at BYU.
leaders.funFact: Among his many Church callings, he once served as a seminary teacher.

leaders.name: Ulisses Soares
leaders.calling: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
leaders.apostleDateNote: Bio: 'sustained to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles on March 31, 2018.'
leaders.formerCareerDetail: He worked as an accountant and auditor for multinational corporations in Brazil and later as director for temporal affairs in the Church's São Paulo area office.
leaders.funFact: He served a mission in Brazil (Rio de Janeiro) and later was president of the Portugal Porto Mission.

leaders.name: Patrick Kearon
leaders.calling: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
leaders.apostleDateNote: Bio gives the call date (December 7, 2023); the later conference sustaining date was not verified.
leaders.formerCareerDetail: He worked in a range of industries in the United Kingdom, Saudi Arabia, and the United States, and ran his own communication consultancy.
leaders.funFact: He joined the Church as an adult, on Christmas Eve 1987.

leaders.name: Gérald Caussé
leaders.calling: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
leaders.apostleDateNote: Called and ordained November 6, 2025 (Newsroom); sustained by Church membership in the solemn assembly April 4, 2026.
leaders.formerCareerDetail: He worked in strategy consulting and the food industry and was managing director of Pomona, a French food distribution company; before the Twelve he was the Church's Presiding Bishop (2015–2025).
leaders.funFact: He is an accomplished pianist and has helped record several piano albums.

leaders.name: Clark G. Gilbert
leaders.calling: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
leaders.apostleDateNote: Called February 11 and ordained February 12, 2026 (Newsroom); sustained by Church membership in the solemn assembly April 4, 2026.
leaders.formerCareerDetail: He was a professor of entrepreneurial management at Harvard and later CEO of the Deseret News and Deseret Digital Media, before leading BYU–Idaho, BYU–Pathway Worldwide, and Church education.
leaders.funFact: He spent most of his childhood in Phoenix, Arizona, served a mission in Japan (Kobe), and he and his wife have eight children.

notes: Recent changes (verified on Church Newsroom / churchofjesuschrist.org): - President Russell M. Nelson died September 27, 2025, age 101 (newsroom.churchofjesuschrist.org/article/president-russell-m-nelson-memorial). - Dallin H. Oaks set apart as 18th President of the Church October 14, 2025, with Henry B. Eyring (First Counselor) and D. Todd Christofferson (Second Counselor); Jeffrey R. Holland became President of the Quorum of the Twelve (newsroom.churchofjesuschrist.org/article/president-oaks-new-first-presidency). - Gerald (official spelling: Gérald) Caussé, then Presiding Bishop, called and ordained an Apostle November 6, 2025 (newsroom.churchofjesuschrist.org/article/gerald-causse-called-quorum-of-the-twelve-apostles). - President Jeffrey R. Holland died December 27, 2025, age 85 (newsroom.churchofjesuschrist.org/article/president-jeffrey-r-holland-memorial). - Dieter F. Uchtdorf set apart as ACTING President of the Quorum of the Twelve January 8, 2026; Henry B. Eyring is the President of the Quorum but serves in the First Presidency (newsroom.churchofjesuschrist.org/article/dieter-f--uchtdorf--new-acting-president-of-the-quorum-of-the-twelve-apostles). - Clark G. Gilbert, Commissioner of Church Education, called February 11 and ordained February 12, 2026 (newsroom.churchofjesuschrist.org/article/clark-gilbert-called-quorum-of-the-twelve-apostles). - April 4, 2026 solemn assembly sustained Eyring as President and Uchtdorf as Acting President of the Twelve, and listed the Twelve in the order used here (churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/04/12christofferson). - No further apostolic deaths or calls found in Newsroom through its Sept 30, 2026 RSS feed; October 2026 general conference is just starting, so recheck after it. Data notes: birthYear/birthplace come from the 'Born' field on each churchofjesuschrist.org/learn bio. Uchtdorf's page header says 'Ostrava, Czech Republic'; the text says Czechoslovakia (the country's name in 1940). Most fun facts come from the bioUrl page; a few come from the funFactSource Newsroom article. formerCareer phrases are short kid-friendly summaries of the bio wording. The portrait URLs are the IIIF images from each bio page's official-portrait , at 700px wide (all returned 200 image/jpeg, about 700x840). Christofferson's and Caussé's are 2025 portraits; Gilbert's was taken in 2026 'as a General Authority'.
